assignments.goal: Adjudicate whether A3's duplicate cache invalidation is a lifecycle product defect or an over-specified test detail by comparing the accepted contract, exact source call graph, and executable semantic restart counts.
assignments.rationale: The accepted A1 contract requires at most one ticker/heartbeat/bus/observer/lock rebuild sequence and zero Send actuation; it does not require exactly one invocation of an idempotent DOM-cache helper. A3 proved ticker, heartbeat, bus/redetect sequencing remained single-gate while cacheClear was 2 because recoverAfterWake clears once directly and reDetect clears again.
assignments.mandatoryAction: Use two opposing interpretations: strict exactly-once invalidation versus bounded idempotent invalidation. Cross-check the accepted lifecycle contract before changing any assertion. Instrument semantic runtime-service counts separately from cache invalidation. Correct the test only if the accepted contract proves the assertion over-specified; otherwise preserve the failure and create a separate builder repair.
acceptanceCriteria: Show from the accepted A1 contract whether exact-once applies to runtime-service rebuilds, cache-helper invocations, or both
Show from source why cacheClear is 2 and whether any DOM-cache consumer exists between the direct clear and reDetect
Preserve an explicit bounded cache-invalidation assertion so future unbounded churn still fails
Keep ticker, heartbeat, bus/redetect and Send-safety assertions exact and unchanged
Run focused lifecycle Jest and both production/adversarial Chromium lifecycle fixtures on an exact guarded head
If corrected tests pass, mark A3/A3X submitted and activate A4; if a product defect remains, block A3X and create the smallest builder repair
assignments.fallbackWork: If exact-head execution cannot be obtained, keep A3X blocked on execution evidence only and preserve the exact guarded command/carrier requirement.
